questions.question: In a row of boys, Rahul is 33rd from the left end. Rajat is 17 ranks to the right of Rahul. If Rajat is 35th from right end, then what will be the rank of Rahul from the right end?
questions.questionHtml: In a row of boys, Rahul is 33rd from the left end. Rajat is 17 ranks to the right of Rahul. If Rajat is 35th from right end, then what will be the rank of Rahul from the right end?
questions.solution:
Rahul’s rank from the left = 33

Rajat’s rank from the right = 35

Rajat’s rank = 17 to the right of Rahul

So, Rajat’s rank from the left = 33 + 17

→ 50

Total students = Rajat’s rank from left + Rajat’s rank from the right – 1

→ 50 + 35 – 1

→ 84

Rahul’s rank from the right = Total students – Rahul’s rank from the left – 1

→ 84 – 33 + 1 = 52

Hence, Rahul’s rank from the right is 52.

questions.questionHtml:
Some equations have been solved based on a certain system. Find the correct answer for the unsolved equation on that basis.

If 167 + 724 = 31, 687 + 153 = 63 then 645 + 384 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern follow is:

167 + 724 = 31; it can be obtained by multiplying first two digits and adding with third digit of every number i.e.,

167 + 724 = (1 × 6 + 7) + (7 × 2 + 4) = 13 + 18 = 31;

Similarly,

687 + 153 = 63;

687 + 153 = (6 × 8 + 7) + (1 × 5 + 3) = 55 + 8 = 63;

Similarly,

645 + 384

645 + 384 = (6 × 4 + 5) + (3 × 8 + 4) = 29 + 28 = 57;

Hence, 645 + 384 = 57 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 784 - 4 + 18 × 16 ÷ 84 = 400
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

784 - 4 + 18 × 16 ÷ 84 = 400
questions.solution:
On checking each options one by one and by interchanging the signs.

1) × and ÷ 

784 - 4 + 18 × 16 ÷ 84

On interchanging,

= 784 - 4 + 18 ÷ 16 × 84

= 784 - 4 + 1.125 × 84

= 784 - 4 + 94.5

= 878.5 - 4

= 874.5 which is not equal to 400

2) - and +

784 - 4 + 18 × 16 ÷ 84

On interchanging,

= 784 + 4 - 18 × 16 ÷ 84

= 784 + 4 - 18 × 0.19

= 784 + 4 - 3.42

= 788 - 3.42

= 784.58 which is not equal to 400

3) - and ÷ 

784 - 4 + 18 × 16 ÷ 84

On interchanging,

= 784 ÷ 4 + 18 × 16 - 84

= 196 + 288 - 84

= 484 - 84 

= 400

Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: If a shopkeeper increases the list price of his product by 20% and then provide 20% discount on the list price, what would be his profit/loss on that product?
questions.questionHtml: If a shopkeeper increases the list price of his product by 20% and then provide 20% discount on the list price, what would be his profit/loss on that product?
questions.solution:
The shopkeeper increases the list price of his product by 20% and then provide 20% discount on the list price.

By formula:

Profit/Loss % = [(% increase in price) × (% decrease in price)] ÷ 100 

= [(+20) × (-20)] ÷ 100  ('+' sign is used to denote increase in price and '-' sign is used to denote discount)

= -400 ÷ 100

= -4%

The negative sign here implies that loss is made.

Therefore, the shopkeeper makes a loss of 4% on the product.

Hence, ‘4% loss’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Evaluate the following expression: |5 × 5 - 4 × 5 ÷ 4 - 28| mod 17
questions.questionHtml:
Evaluate the following expression:

|5 × 5 - 4 × 5 ÷ 4 - 28| mod 17
questions.solution:
Given:

|5 × 5 - 4 × 5 ÷ 4 - 28| mod 17

→ |5 × 5 - 4 × 5 ÷ 4 - 28| mod 17

→ |5 × 5 - 4 × 1.25 - 28| mod 17

→ |25 - 5 - 28| mod 17

→ |-8| mod 17

→ 8 mod 17

= 8

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2."

Confusion PointsAbsolute Value (| |): This symbol makes any number inside it positive.
For example, | -7 | becomes 7, and | 7 | remains 7. It represents the distance of a number from zero on a number line.

Modulo (mod): This operation finds the remainder after division.

For example, 7 mod 6 means what is the remainder when 7 is divided by 6? The answer is 1.
Similarly, 10 mod 5 means what is the remainder when 10 is divided by 5? The answer is 0 because 10 divides exactly by 5 with no remainder.

Key Points

  • The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, added the eleventh fundamental duty to the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.
  • This amendment emphasizes the duty of every citizen to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
  • It was introduced alongside the insertion of Article 21A, which made education a fundamental right for children in the specified age group.
  • The eleventh fundamental duty was added to ensure active participation in the realization of the Right to Education (RTE).
  • The amendment aligns with the Directive Principles of State Policy and aims to promote inclusive education across India.

Additional Information

  • Article 51A - Fundamental Duties
    • Fundamental duties were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, under the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
    • Initially, there were 10 fundamental duties listed under Article 51A.
    • The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added the eleventh duty related to education.
    • Fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning citizens cannot be legally compelled to perform them.
  • Right to Education (Article 21A)
    • Article 21A was introduced by the 86th Amendment Act, making free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
    • It mandates the state to provide education to all children in this age group.
    • The Right to Education Act, 2009, was enacted to operationalize this provision.
    • This initiative aims to reduce illiteracy and empower children through education.
  • Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)
    • DPSPs are guidelines for the government to establish a social order based on justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
    • Article 45 of the DPSP initially stated that the State should provide free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 years.
    • Article 21A and the eleventh fundamental duty are direct advancements of this directive.
    • These principles are not enforceable by law but serve as a framework for policymaking.

questions.question: Arrange the following Gandhian movements in chronological order: Champaran Satyagraha Non-Cooperation Movement Salt March Quit India Movement Options:
questions.questionHtml:
Arrange the following Gandhian movements in chronological order:

  1. Champaran Satyagraha
  2. Non-Cooperation Movement
  3. Salt March
  4. Quit India Movement

Options:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 'a) 1, 2, 3, 4.'

Key Points

  • Champaran Satyagraha (1917):
    • This movement was Gandhi's first significant involvement in Indian politics.
    • It addressed the grievances of indigo farmers in Bihar against oppressive policies of British planters.
    • Gandhi's successful intervention marked the beginning of mass mobilization against British rule.
  • Non-Cooperation Movement (1920):
    • This movement followed the Champaran Satyagraha and aimed to resist British rule through non-violent means.
    • It was launched in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and included a nationwide boycott of British goods and institutions.
  • Salt March (1930):
    • Also known as the Dandi March, this was a key act of civil disobedience against the British salt tax.
    • Gandhi led a 240-mile march to the Arabian Sea to produce salt from seawater, symbolizing the right to self-governance.
  • Quit India Movement (1942):
    • Launched during World War II, this movement demanded an end to British rule in India.
    • It called for immediate independence and involved mass protests, leading to the arrest of many leaders, including Gandhi.

Hence, the correct chronological order is:

  • 1. Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
  • 2. Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
  • 3. Salt March (1930)
  • 4. Quit India Movement (1942)

Hence, the correct answer is: a) 1, 2, 3, 4.

Additional Information

  • Key Features of Gandhian Movements:
    • Champaran Satyagraha: Focused on the rights of peasants and set the tone for future movements.
    • Non-Cooperation Movement: Established the principle of mass non-violent resistance against colonial rule.
    • Salt March: A significant act of civil disobedience that highlighted the unjust laws imposed by the British.
    • Quit India Movement: Marked a turning point in the freedom struggle, showcasing widespread dissatisfaction with British rule.
  • Impact on Indian Independence:
    • These movements were pivotal in uniting Indians against colonial oppression and fostering a sense of national identity.
    • They collectively demonstrated the effectiveness of non-violent resistance in the struggle for independence.

questions.question: A device which converts chemical energy into electrical energy is called
questions.questionHtml: A device which converts chemical energy into electrical energy is called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Battery.

Key Points

  • A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy.
  • The chemical reactions in a battery involve the flow of electrons from one material (electrode) to another, through an external circuit.
    • Energy using an electrochemical oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction.
  • The flow of electrons provides an electric current that can be used to do work.

Additional Information

Motor
  • Convert Electrical energy into Mechanical energy.
  • It works on Fleming's left-hand rule.

Dynamo
  • Convert Mechanical energy into Electrical energy.

Generator
  • Convert Mechanical energy into Electrical energy.
  • It works on Fleming's right-hand rule.
Moving coil meter
  • Measuring a small electrical current or a function of the current by deflection of a moving coil.
  • The deflection is a mechanical rotation derived from forces resulting from the current.
  • Example: Galvanometer.

Important Points

  • Fleming's right-hand rule (generators): It shows the direction of induced current when a conductor attached to a circuit moves in a magnetic field. It can be used to determine the direction of current in a generator's windings.
    • The thumb is pointed in the direction of the motion of the conductor relative to the magnetic field.
    • The first finger is pointed in the direction of the magnetic field. (North to south).
    • Then the second finger represents the direction of the induced or generated current within the conductor (from the terminal with lower electric potential to the terminal with higher electric potential, as in a voltage source).
  • Fleming's left-hand rule (electric motors): When current flows through a conducting wire, and an external magnetic field is applied across that flow, the conducting wire experiences a force perpendicular both to that field and to the direction of the current flow (i.e. they are mutually perpendicular).
    • The Thumb represents the direction of the Thrust on the conductor / Motion of the Conductor.
    • The Forefinger represents the direction of the Magnetic Field.
    • The Centre finger represents the direction of the Current.

questions.question: If \(x+\frac{1}{x}=\sqrt{13}\) , then one of the values \(x^3-\frac{1}{x^3}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(x+\frac{1}{x}=\sqrt{13}\), then one of the values \(x^3-\frac{1}{x^3}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x + 1/x = k, then x − 1/x = √(k2 − 4).

Here, k = √13, so x − 1/x = √(13 − 4) = √9 = 3.

If x − 1/x = a, then x3 − 1/x3 = a3 + 3a.

Substituting a = 3, we get: 33 + 3 × 3 = 27 + 9 = 36.

∴ The correct answer is 36.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + 1/x = √13

Formula Used:

(a − b)2 = (a + b)2 − 4ab

a3 − b3 = (a − b)3 + 3ab(a − b)

Calculations:

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = (x + 1/x)2 − 4(x)(1/x)

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = (√13)2 − 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = 13 − 4 = 9

⇒ x − 1/x = ±3

Taking x − 1/x = 3 (since the positive value matches the given options):

⇒ x3 − 1/x3 = (x − 1/x)3 + 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ x3 − 1/x3 = 33 + 3 × 3

⇒ x3 − 1/x3 = 27 + 9 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36.

Additional Information

Sum of Squares Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. This is derived directly from expanding the whole square formula (x + 1/x)2.

Difference of Squares Transition

The relationship between the sum and difference of reciprocal terms is given by the identity (x + 1/x)2 − (x − 1/x)2 = 4.

Sum of Cubes Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k. This comes from rearranging the expansion of (x + 1/x)3.

Difference of Cubes Identity

If x − 1/x = k, then x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k. This is an essential shortcut for quickly solving differences of cubed terms in algebra.

Given TSA = 6πr2 = 231 ⇒ r2 = 231 × 7 ÷ (6 × 22) = 49/4 ⇒ r = 7/2 cm.

Height h = 2 × (7/2) = 7 cm.

Volume = πr2h = (22/7) × (49/4) × 7 = 269.5 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 231 cm2

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2/3 of TSA

Formula Used:

TSA = 2πr(r + h)

CSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ CSA = (2/3) × 231 = 154 cm2

⇒ We know that, TSA = CSA + 2 × Area of Base

⇒ 231 = 154 + 2πr2

⇒ 2πr2 = 231 − 154 = 77

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r2 = 77

⇒ (44/7) × r2 = 77

⇒ r2 = (77 × 7) ÷ 44 = 49/4

⇒ r = 7/2 = 3.5 cm

⇒ Now, substitute r in the CSA formula:

⇒ 2πrh = 154

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × h = 154

⇒ 22 × h = 154

⇒ h = 154 ÷ 22 = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of cylinder = πr2h

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2) × 7

⇒ Volume = 11 × 7 × 7 ÷ 2 = 539 ÷ 2 = 269.5 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cm3.

Additional Information

Cylinder Surface Areas

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder is 2πrh. The Total Surface Area (TSA) includes the two circular bases, calculated as 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume represents the total 3D space enclosed and is given by πr2h, where r is the base radius and h is the height.

Relation to a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third the volume of the cylinder (Volume = 1/3 × πr2h).

questions.question: The external radius and internal radius of a hollow cylinder are 42 cm and 36 cm and its length is 56 cm. If we put two hollow cones of a height of 28 cm one on the top and one on the bottom then what will be the volume of the material used to make the structure? Given the external and internal radius of the cone is the same as the cylinder.
questions.questionHtml: The external radius and internal radius of a hollow cylinder are 42 cm and 36 cm and its length is 56 cm. If we put two hollow cones of a height of 28 cm one on the top and one on the bottom then what will be the volume of the material used to make the structure? Given the external and internal radius of the cone is the same as the cylinder.

options.html: 108924 cm3
109856 cm3
109843 cm3
109824 cm3

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the volume formulas for both the cylinder and cones involve π (≈ 22⁄7), the total final volume must be a multiple of 11.

We can quickly use the divisibility rule of 11 (difference between the sum of alternating digits) on the given options:

⇒ 108924 → (1 + 8 + 2) − (0 + 9 + 4) = 11 − 13 = −2 (Not divisible)

⇒ 109856 → (1 + 9 + 5) − (0 + 8 + 6) = 15 − 14 = 1 (Not divisible)

⇒ 109824 → (1 + 9 + 2) − (0 + 8 + 4) = 12 − 12 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

Only 109824 is perfectly divisible by 11.

∴ The correct answer is 109824 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ External radius (R) = 42 cm

⇒ Internal radius (r) = 36 cm

⇒ Height of the hollow cylinder (H) = 56 cm

⇒ Height of each hollow cone (h) = 28 cm

Formula Used:

⇒ Volume of hollow cylinder = π(R2 − r2)H

⇒ Volume of a hollow cone = 1⁄3 × π(R2 − r2)h

Calculations:

⇒ Total material volume = Volume of hollow cylinder + (2 × Volume of hollow cone)

⇒ Total volume = π(R2 − r2)H + 2 × [ 1⁄3 × π(R2 − r2)h ]

⇒ Total volume = π(R2 − r2) × [ H + 2h⁄3 ]

⇒ R2 − r2 = 422 − 362

⇒ R2 − r2 = (42 + 36) × (42 − 36) = 78 × 6 = 468 cm2

⇒ Total volume = 22⁄7 × 468 × [ 56 + (2 × 28) ÷ 3 ]

⇒ Total volume = 22⁄7 × 468 × [ 56 + 56⁄3 ]

⇒ Total volume = 22⁄7 × 468 × [ 224⁄3 ]

⇒ Total volume = 22 × (468 ÷ 3) × (224 ÷ 7)

⇒ Total volume = 22 × 156 × 32

⇒ Total volume = 109824 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 109824 cm3.

Additional Information

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

The volume of material used in a hollow cylindrical tube is given by V = π(R2 − r2)H. It essentially subtracts the empty inner volume from the total outer volume.

Divisibility Rule of 11 in Geometry

In mensuration problems involving circular cross-sections (spheres, cones, cylinders), the final resulting quantity will frequently be a multiple of 11 due to the involvement of π (≈ 22⁄7). Leveraging this allows for rapid elimination of options without calculating the final product.

Total Surface Area of a Hollow Cylinder

The Total Surface Area involves the outer curved surface, the inner curved surface, and the two top/bottom circular rings: TSA = 2πRH + 2πrH + 2π(R2 − r2).

questions.question: If the sugar price is increased by 25% by how much percent consumption should be reduced that expense remains same.
questions.questionHtml: If the sugar price is increased by 25% by how much percent consumption should be reduced that expense remains same.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Fractional equivalent of 25% increase = +1/4

To keep the expenditure constant, the consumption must be reduced by the ratio: −1 ÷ (4 + 1) = −1/5

Percentage reduction = (1/5) × 100% = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Increase in the price of sugar = 25%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Reduction % = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100% (where R is the percentage increase)

Calculations:

⇒ Let initial price = 100 units and initial consumption = 100 units.

⇒ Initial expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10000 units.

⇒ New price after 25% increase = 100 + 25 = 125 units.

⇒ Let the new consumption be C.

⇒ To keep expenditure constant: 125 × C = 10000

⇒ C = 10000 ÷ 125 = 80 units.

⇒ Decrease in consumption = 100 − 80 = 20 units.

⇒ Percentage reduction = (20 ÷ 100) × 100% = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Price and Consumption Rule

When Expenditure is constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional. An increase in price leads to a proportional decrease in consumption.

Percentage Increase / Decrease Concept

If value A is R% more than B, then B is less than A by exactly [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%.

Standard Fractional Equivalents

1/2 = 50%, 1/3 = 33.33%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/6 ≈ 16.66%.

questions.question: The tops of two poles of height 30 m and 14 m are connected by a string. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, find the length of the wire.
questions.questionHtml: The tops of two poles of height 30 m and 14 m are connected by a string. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, find the length of the wire.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Vertical difference in heights = 30 − 14 = 16 m.

This difference acts as the perpendicular in the right-angled triangle formed with the wire.

Using sin(30°) = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

⇒ 1/2 = 16 / Length of wire

⇒ Length of wire = 16 × 2 = 32 m.

∴ The correct answer is 32 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the taller pole (AB) = 30 m

Height of the shorter pole (CD) = 14 m

Angle made by the string with the horizontal (∠ACE) = 30°

Formula Used:

sin(θ) = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

Calculations:

⇒ Let the horizontal line from C meet AB at E.

⇒ CE is parallel to the ground BD, so EB = CD = 14 m.

⇒ The length of the upper part of the taller pole AE = AB − EB

⇒ AE = 30 − 14 = 16 m

⇒ In right-angled triangle AEC, sin(30°) = AE / AC

⇒ 1/2 = 16 / AC

⇒ AC = 16 × 2 = 32 m

∴ The correct answer is 32 m.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios

In any right-angled triangle, sin(θ) = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, cos(θ) = Base / Hypotenuse, and tan(θ) = Perpendicular / Base.

Angles of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation is the angle between the horizontal line and the upward line of sight. The angle of depression is formed when looking downwards. Both act as alternate interior angles and are always equal.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: H2 = P2 + B2.

questions.question: A tank is 25 m long, 12 m wide and 6 m deep. The cost (in Rs) of plastering its walls and bottom at Rs. 10 per m 2 is:
questions.questionHtml: A tank is 25 m long, 12 m wide and 6 m deep. The cost (in Rs) of plastering its walls and bottom at Rs. 10 per m<sup>2 </sup>is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Plastering Area = Area of bottom + Area of 4 walls

⇒ Area = (l × b) + 2h(l + b)

⇒ Area = (25 × 12) + 2 × 6 × (25 + 12)

⇒ Area = 300 + 12 × 37 = 744 m2

Cost = 744 × 10 = 7440

∴ The correct answer is ₹7440.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length (l) = 25 m, Width (b) = 12 m, Depth (h) = 6 m

Rate of plastering = ₹10 per m2

Formula Used:

Area of 4 walls = Lateral Surface Area = 2h(l + b)

Area of bottom = l × b

Total area to be plastered = 2h(l + b) + (l × b)

Calculation:

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 2 × 6 × (25 + 12)

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 12 × 37 = 444 m2

⇒ Area of bottom = 25 × 12 = 300 m2

⇒ Total area = 444 + 300 = 744 m2

⇒ Total cost = 744 × 10 = 7440

∴ The correct answer is ₹7440.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area includes all 6 faces: TSA = 2(lb + bh + lh).

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as: Volume = l × b × h.

Longest Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest pole that can be placed in a room is its diagonal: d = √(l2 + b2 + h2).

questions.question: \(\rm \frac{{1\, + \,2\,{{\cot }^2}\left( {90\, - \,x} \right)\, - \,2\cos ec\left( {90\, - \,x} \right) \cdot \cot \left( {90\, - \,x} \right)}}{{\cos ec\left( {90\, - \,x} \right)\, - \,\cot \left( {90\, - \,x} \right)}}\, = \,?\)
questions.questionHtml: \(\rm \frac{{1\, + \,2\,{{\cot }^2}\left( {90\, - \,x} \right)\, - \,2\cos ec\left( {90\, - \,x} \right) \cdot \cot \left( {90\, - \,x} \right)}}{{\cos ec\left( {90\, - \,x} \right)\, - \,\cot \left( {90\, - \,x} \right)}}\, = \,?\)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put x = 45° in the given expression: [1 + 2cot2(90° − 45°) − 2cosec(90° − 45°) × cot(90° − 45°)] ÷ [cosec(90° − 45°) − cot(90° − 45°)]

⇒ [1 + 2(1)2 − 2(√2)(1)] ÷ [√2 − 1] = (3 − 2√2) ÷ (√2 − 1)

Rationalizing by multiplying with (√2 + 1): (3 − 2√2)(√2 + 1) = 3√2 + 3 − 4 − 2√2 = √2 − 1

Checking options at x = 45°, we find sec 45° − tan 45° = √2 − 1, which matches exactly.

∴ The correct answer is sec x − tan x.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = [1 + 2cot2(90° − x) − 2cosec(90° − x) × cot(90° − x)] ÷ [cosec(90° − x) − cot(90° − x)]

Formula Used:

⇒ cot(90° − x) = tan x

⇒ cosec(90° − x) = sec x

⇒ 1 + tan2 x = sec2 x

⇒ a2 + b2 − 2ab = (a − b)2

Calculation:

⇒ Expression = [1 + 2tan2 x − 2sec x × tan x] ÷ [sec x − tan x]

⇒ Expression = [(1 + tan2 x) + tan2 x − 2sec x × tan x] ÷ [sec x − tan x]

⇒ Replace (1 + tan2 x) with sec2 x in the numerator:

⇒ Expression = [sec2 x + tan2 x − 2sec x × tan x] ÷ [sec x − tan x]

⇒ Expression = (sec x − tan x)2 ÷ (sec x − tan x)

⇒ Expression = sec x − tan x

∴ The correct answer is sec x − tan x.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Identities

sin(90° − x) = cos x, tan(90° − x) = cot x, and sec(90° − x) = cosec x.

Pythagorean Identities

sin2x + cos2x = 1, 1 + tan2x = sec2x, and 1 + cot2x = cosec2x.

Algebraic Identities in Trigonometry

(a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2 can be applied directly to simplify complex fractional trigonometric expressions.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle are 20 meters and 12 meters respectively. If the perimeter of the rectangle is equal to the area of a square, then what is the perimeter of the square?
questions.questionHtml: The length and breadth of a rectangle are 20 meters and 12 meters respectively. If the perimeter of the rectangle is equal to the area of a square, then what is the perimeter of the square?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (20 + 12) = 64 m

Area of Square = Perimeter of Rectangle = 64 m2

Side of Square = √64 = 8 m

Perimeter of Square = 4 × 8 = 32 m

∴ The correct answer is 32 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the rectangle (L) = 20 m

Breadth of the rectangle (B) = 12 m

Formula Used:

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (L + B)

Area of a square = a2 (where a is the side of the square)

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a

Calculations:

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangle = 2 × (20 + 12)

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangle = 2 × 32 = 64 m

⇒ According to the question, Area of the square = Perimeter of the rectangle

⇒ a2 = 64

⇒ a = √64 = 8 m

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × 8 = 32 m

∴ The correct answer is 32 m.

Additional Information

Properties of a Rectangle

A rectangle has opposite sides that are equal and parallel. All interior angles are exactly 90°. The diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Area = L × B, and Diagonal = √(L2 + B2).

Properties of a Square

A square is a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. The diagonals intersect at right angles (90°). Area = a2, Diagonal = a√2, and Perimeter = 4 × a.

Parallelogram

A quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel and equal. Area = Base × Height. Both squares and rectangles are specific types of parallelograms.

questions.question: The virus count in a culture decreases at the rate of 5% per hour due to a medicine. If the virus count in the culture at 11.00 a.m. was 2.3 × 10 7 , find the virus count at 1.00 p.m. on the same day.
questions.questionHtml: The virus count in a culture decreases at the rate of 5% per hour due to a medicine. If the virus count in the culture at 11.00 a.m. was 2.3 × 10<sup>7</sup>, find the virus count at 1.00 p.m. on the same day.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net percentage decrease for 2 hours at 5% per hour = −5 − 5 + (5 × 5) ÷ 100 = −9.75%

Remaining percentage of virus count = 100% − 9.75% = 90.25%

Final count = 2.3 × 107 × 90.25% = 2.07575 × 107 ≈ 2.076 × 107

∴ The correct answer is 2.076 × 107.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial virus count at 11:00 a.m. (P) = 2.3 × 107

Rate of decrease (R) = 5% per hour

Time duration from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. (n) = 2 hours

Formula Used:

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ Final virus count = 2.3 × 107 × (1 − 5/100)2

⇒ Final virus count = 2.3 × 107 × (1 − 1/20)2

⇒ Final virus count = 2.3 × 107 × (19/20) × (19/20)

⇒ Final virus count = 2.3 × 107 × (361/400)

⇒ Final virus count = 2.3 × 107 × 0.9025

⇒ Final virus count = 2.07575 × 107

⇒ Final virus count ≈ 2.076 × 107

∴ The correct answer is 2.076 × 107.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes successively by a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by a + b + (a × b)/100. For decreases, use negative values for a and b.

Depreciation Formula

If the present value of a quantity is P and it depreciates at a rate of R% per period, the value after n periods is A = P × (1 − R/100)n.

Fraction Multiplying Factor

A decrease of R% corresponds to a multiplying factor of (100 − R)/100. For a 5% decrease, the direct multiplying factor is 95/100 or 19/20.

questions.question: If Ram's age is 1/3 times Rohan's age and Ravi's age is 5/2 times Ram's age. The average age of Ram, Ravi, and Rohan are 52 years. Then the difference between Ram's age and Rohan's age is
questions.questionHtml: If Ram's age is 1/3 times Rohan's age and Ravi's age is 5/2 times  Ram's age. The average age of Ram, Ravi, and Rohan are 52 years. Then the difference between Ram's age and Rohan's age is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Ram : Rohan : Ravi = 2 : 6 : 5 (since Ram is 1/3 of Rohan and 2/5 of Ravi).

Total parts = 2 + 6 + 5 = 13 parts.

Total sum of their ages = Average × 3 = 52 × 3 = 156 years.

1 part = 156 ÷ 13 = 12 years.

Difference between Rohan and Ram = 6 − 2 = 4 parts = 4 × 12 = 48 years.

∴ The correct answer is 48 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Ram's age = 1/3 × Rohan's age ⇒ Rohan's age = 3 × Ram's age

⇒ Ravi's age = 5/2 × Ram's age

Calculations:

⇒ The ratio of ages of Ram : Rohan : Ravi = Ram : 3 × Ram : 5/2 × Ram = 2 : 6 : 5

⇒ Let the ages of Ram, Rohan, and Ravi be 2x, 6x, and 5x respectively.

⇒ Average age of all three = (2x + 6x + 5x) ÷ 3 = 13x / 3

⇒ We are given that the average age is 52 years.

⇒ 13x / 3 = 52

⇒ 13x = 156

⇒ x = 12

⇒ Age of Ram = 2x = 2 × 12 = 24 years.

⇒ Age of Rohan = 6x = 6 × 12 = 72 years.

⇒ Difference between Rohan's age and Ram's age = 72 − 24 = 48 years.

∴ The correct answer is 48 years.

Additional Information

Ratio Combination

If A : B = x : y and A : C = x : z, then the combined ratio is A : B : C = x : y : z. Making the common term equal helps to simplify and compare multiple relationships directly.

Average Concept

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations. Hence, the total sum can always be found using Sum = Average × Total number.

Age Difference

The age difference between any two people always remains constant throughout their lifetime, regardless of the number of years passed or to come.

questions.question: X and Y can do a piece of work in 45 days and 40 days respectively. They begin to work together, but X leaves after n days and then Y completes the remaining work in 23 days. What is n equal to ?
questions.questionHtml: X and Y can do a piece of work in 45 days and 40 days respectively. They begin to work together, but X leaves after n days and then Y completes the remaining work in 23 days. What is n equal to ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work = LCM of 45 and 40 = 360 units.

Efficiency of X = 360 ÷ 45 = 8 units/day | Efficiency of Y = 360 ÷ 40 = 9 units/day.

Work done by Y alone in the last 23 days = 23 × 9 = 207 units.

Remaining work done by X and Y together = 360 − 207 = 153 units.

Combined efficiency = 8 + 9 = 17 units/day ⇒ n = 153 ÷ 17 = 9.

∴ The correct answer is n = 9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by X to complete the work = 45 days.

Time taken by Y to complete the work = 40 days.

X and Y work together for n days, and Y completes the remaining work in 23 days.

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of given days.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
X 45 360 8
Y 40 9

Calculations:

⇒ Combined efficiency of X and Y = 8 + 9 = 17 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by Y alone in 23 days = 23 × 9 = 207 units.

⇒ Remaining work done by X and Y together = Total Work − Work done by Y alone.

⇒ Remaining work = 360 − 207 = 153 units.

⇒ Time taken by X and Y to complete 153 units (n) = 153 ÷ 17 = 9 days.

⇒ Hence, n = 9.

∴ The correct answer is n = 9.

Additional Information

LCM Method in Time and Work

Total work is considered to be the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the distinct days taken by the individuals to complete the job. Efficiency of a person is given by: Total Work ÷ Time Taken.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, the wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept remains similar to time and work, with the only variation being that an inlet pipe does positive work (filling) while an outlet or leakage pipe does negative work (emptying).

questions.question: Average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If average weight of A and B is 35 kg and that of B and C is 48 kg. The weight of A is?
questions.questionHtml: Average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. If average weight of A and B is 35 kg and that of B and C is 48 kg. The weight of A is?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total weight of A, B, and C = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

Total weight of B and C = 48 × 2 = 96 kg

Weight of A = Total weight of (A + B + C) − Total weight of (B + C)

⇒ Weight of A = 135 − 96 = 39 kg

∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average weight of A, B and C = 45 kg

Average weight of A and B = 35 kg

Average weight of B and C = 48 kg

Formula Used:

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of weights of A, B and C = 45 × 3 = 135 kg

⇒ Sum of weights of A and B = 35 × 2 = 70 kg

⇒ Sum of weights of B and C = 48 × 2 = 96 kg

⇒ We know that (A + B + C) = 135

⇒ Substituting the value of (B + C) in the above equation:

⇒ A + 96 = 135

⇒ A = 135 − 96 = 39 kg

∴ The correct answer is 39 kg.

Additional Information

Average Formula

The average of a set of numbers is their sum divided by the total number of items in that set. Formula: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

Combined Average

If the average of a group of n1 observations is a1 and that of n2 observations is a2, then the combined average is calculated as (n1 × a1 + n2 × a2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Weighted Average

When values carry different levels of importance, the weighted average is calculated by multiplying each value by its weight, summing these products, and dividing by the overall sum of the weights.

questions.question: The speed of the stream is 4 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 40 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">The speed of the stream is 4 km/h. A boat can cover a distance of 40 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 4 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).</font></font>
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For such quadratic equation problems, checking the options is the fastest method.

Total time = [Downstream distance ÷ (v + u)] + [Upstream distance ÷ (v − u)]

⇒ 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4) = 4

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

Checking Option 4: Put v = 12 ⇒ 10 / 16 + 3 / 8 = 5 / 8 + 3 / 8 = 1. (Condition is satisfied)

∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of stream (u) = 4 km/h

Downstream distance = 40 km

Upstream distance = 12 km

Total Time = 4 hours

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) + Speed of stream (u)

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat in still water (v) − Speed of stream (u)

Calculations:

⇒ Total Time = (40 ÷ (v + 4)) + (12 ÷ (v − 4))

⇒ 4 = 40 / (v + 4) + 12 / (v − 4)

Dividing the entire equation by 4:

⇒ 10 / (v + 4) + 3 / (v − 4) = 1

⇒ [10(v − 4) + 3(v + 4)] ÷ [(v + 4)(v − 4)] = 1

⇒ 10v − 40 + 3v + 12 = v2 − 16

⇒ 13v − 28 = v2 − 16

⇒ v2 − 13v + 12 = 0

⇒ v2 − 12v − v + 12 = 0

⇒ v(v − 12) − 1(v − 12) = 0

⇒ (v − 12)(v − 1) = 0

Thus, v = 12 or v = 1.

Since the boat is able to travel upstream against a 4 km/h stream, its speed must be greater than the stream speed (v > 4).

⇒ v = 12 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 12 km/h.

Additional Information

Speed of Boat and Stream

If downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

The velocity of the current or stream can be calculated as = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Equal Distance

When a boat travels equal distances upstream and downstream, the Average Speed over the entire journey = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: The population of a country has been growing at a rate of 4% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1,58,18,400, what was the population of the country in 2000?
questions.questionHtml: The population of a country has been growing at a rate of 4% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1,58,18,400, what was the population of the country in 2000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiplying factor for 4% growth = 1 + (4/100) = 104/100 = 26/25.

Number of decades from 2000 to 2030 is 3, so the total compounding factor is (26/25)3 = 17576/15625.

Initial Population = Final Population × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ Initial Population = 1,58,18,400 × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ Initial Population = 900 × 15625 = 1,40,62,500

∴ The correct answer is 1,40,62,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Projected population in 2030 (A) = 1,58,18,400

Growth rate (R) = 4% per decade

Time period (n) = (2030 − 2000) ÷ 10 = 3 decades

Formula Used:

A = P × (1 + R/100)n

Where A is the final population, P is the initial population, R is the rate of growth, and n is the time period.

Calculations:

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (1 + 4/100)3

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (104/100)3

⇒ 1,58,18,400 = P × (26/25)3

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (25/26) × (25/26) × (25/26)

⇒ P = 1,58,18,400 × (15625 / 17576)

⇒ P = 900 × 15625

⇒ P = 1,40,62,500

∴ The correct answer is 1,40,62,500.

Additional Information

Compound Population Growth

When a population grows at a constant rate R over a certain period, it increases exponentially in a manner identical to compound interest. The standard formula applied is Final Population = Initial Population × (1 + R/100)n.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases consistently by a certain percentage R over a period (such as due to mortality or migration), the decay formula becomes Final Population = Initial Population × (1 − R/100)n.

Successive Percentage Change

When the population grows or shrinks at varying rates (R1%, R2%, R3%) in successive time periods, the net final population is calculated as P × (1 ± R1/100) × (1 ± R2/100) × (1 ± R3/100).

questions.question: Two trains started at the same time, one from A to B and other from B to A. They arrive at B and A respectively in 2 hours and 8 hours after they pass each other, what is the ratio of speeds of the two trains?
questions.questionHtml: Two trains started at the same time, one from A to B and other from B to A. They arrive at B and A respectively in 2 hours and 8 hours after they pass each other, what is the ratio of speeds of the two trains?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When two objects move towards each other and take t1 and t2 hours to reach their destinations after crossing:

Speed Ratio (S1 : S2) = √(t2 ÷ t1)

Given, t1 = 2 hours and t2 = 8 hours.

Speed Ratio = √(8 ÷ 2) = √4 = 2 : 1

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Train 1 to reach B after meeting, t1 = 2 hours.

Time taken by Train 2 to reach A after meeting, t2 = 8 hours.

Formula Used:

If two trains start simultaneously from points A and B towards each other and after crossing take t1 and t2 time to reach their respective destinations, then:

S1 ÷ S2 = √(t2 ÷ t1)

Calculations:

⇒ S1 ÷ S2 = √(8 ÷ 2)

⇒ S1 ÷ S2 = √4

⇒ S1 ÷ S2 = 2 ÷ 1

⇒ S1 : S2 = 2 : 1

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.

Additional Information

Meeting Point Distance Ratio

When two objects start at the same time, the distance traveled by them until they meet is directly proportional to their speeds (D1 ÷ D2 = S1 ÷ S2).

Total Time to Meet

If they take t1 and t2 times to reach their respective destinations after meeting, the total time taken to meet is given by t = √(t1 × t2).

Relative Speed

For objects moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is S1 + S2. For objects moving in the same direction, it is S1 − S2.

  • The given sentence refers to a hypothetical situation during the vacuum-sealing process. The phrase “should change” is slightly awkward and can be improved for better readability and correctness.
  • The phrase “Should any of the parameters change” is a more formal and concise way to express the conditional idea.
  • This structure is correct and commonly used in technical or formal contexts, where the possibility of a change is being anticipated.

Correct sentence: Should any of the parameters change unexpectedly during the vacuum-sealing process, the automated system is programmed to initiate an immediate emergency shutdown.

Additional Information

  • Using “Should”:
    • Structure: “Should + subject + base verb” is often used for conditional sentences in formal writing.
    • Example: Should you need assistance, please contact support.
    • Usage: Suggests a hypothetical or possible situation in a polite and formal manner.
  • Other Incorrect Options Explained:
    • Option 2: “If any of the parameters shall change” is incorrect because “shall” is not appropriate for a conditional sentence.
    • Option 3: “If any of the parameters should have changed” indicates a past condition, which does not fit the context of the sentence referring to an ongoing process.
    • Option 4: “No improvement needed” is incorrect as the sentence can be improved for clarity and formality.

Key Points

  • The sentence uses the correlative conjunction not only...but also, which requires parallelism in the sentence structure.

Additional Information

  • Parallelism:
    • Parallelism requires that elements in a sentence that are joined by conjunctions (e.g., "and," "or," "but also") must be in the same grammatical form.
    • Example: "She likes reading, writing, and painting" (all gerunds).
  • Common Errors in Parallelism:
    • Mixing verb forms: "He likes to swim and running" (Incorrect).
    • Corrected version: "He likes to swim and to run" or "He likes swimming and running."

questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence/paragraph are given below. While the first and the last parts (A and F) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence/paragraph.

A. I am not an early riser.

B. But all my excitement was gone the next morning as it was 8 in the morning when I woke up.

C. It was pleasant to see the sun rising in the sky, birds chirping on the branches of trees.

D. The experience was so awesome that I decided to wake up early every morning.

E. By chance, one fine Sunday morning I woke up at 5.

F. I still enjoy sleeping till late and could never turn myself to an early-riser.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "E, C, D, B".

Key Points

  • Sentence A comes at the opening of the paragraph.
  • Sentence E is the second sentence as it states that by chance, one fine Sunday morning I woke up at 5.
  • Sentence C is the third sentence and states that it was pleasant to see the sun rising in the sky, and birds chirping on the branches of trees.
  • Sentence D is the fourth sentence which states that the experience was so awesome that I decided to wake up early every morning.
  • Sentence B is the fifth sentence which states - But all my excitement was gone the next morning as it was 8 in the morning when I woke up.
  • Sentence F comes in last.

Additional Information

  • This is the correct sequence:
  •   I am not an early riser. By chance, one fine Sunday morning I woke up at 5. It was pleasant to see the sun rising in the sky, and birds chirping on the branches of trees. The experience was so awesome that I decided to wake up early every morning. But all my excitement was gone the next morning as it was 8 in the morning when I woke up. I still enjoy sleeping till late and could never turn myself into an early riser.
